title: Adaptive traffic splitter and statistical sentry for model-variant experiments
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Teams need a safe, low-friction way to run model-variant A/B tests, canary rollouts and shadow evaluations that automatically limit exposure, surface regressions early, and trigger deterministic rollback when statistical or safety thresholds are violated. Current manual workflows are slow, risk-prone, and inconsistently instrumented across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.

Objective: Build an "adaptive traffic splitter" service + "statistical sentry" that together let PM/Eng define experiments declaratively (traffic schedule, cohorts, metrics, stopping rules) and then run them safely with: staged exposure, automated sequential statistical checks, multi-metric decision rules, and auto-rollback + audit trail. Integrate with Console for visibility and with the runtime for enforcement.

Key features: 1) Experiment spec (JSON) with variants, traffic allocation schedule (time or request-count based), cohorts, and metric definitions (primary, secondary, safety). 2) Runtime traffic controller that enforces allocations at the router level (supports shadowing and mirrored traffic). 3) Statistical sentry implementing sequential analysis (alpha-spending / group sequential and Bayesian alternatives), with configurable stopping boundaries and minimum sample counts. 4) Multi-metric decision logic with priority/weighting: e.g., primary metric = model-quality (regression rate), safety metrics (toxicity/hallucination) act as veto gates. 5) Auto-rollback action that executes deterministic rollback (single command) and records an incident with root-cause artifacts. 6) Observability: prebuilt dashboards, export to metrics store, per-variant traces, and diff visualizations (latency, cost-per-token, quality). 7) Audit & compliance: immutable experiment run log, exposure consent, and exportable evidence for customers.

Statistical approach: Support two analysis modes: frequentist sequential tests (alpha spending - O'Brien-Fleming / Pocock) and a Bayesian sequential monitor (posterior probability of improvement > X). Default safe mode: conservative alpha-spending with a one-sided threshold and a safety veto on any safety metric breaching a configured tolerance for two consecutive windows. The sentry should track lookback windows by time and by effective sample size (requests with sufficient tokens).

Implementation considerations: - Traffic skew: ensure router samples uniformly across user segments; provide cohort-aware bucketing to avoid confounding. - KV cache and prefix caching can bias quality metrics; include a sampling transform to exclude responses hitting cold cache windows or to stratify by cache-hit. - Shadow traffic: ensure rate-limited shadowing and no downstream side-effects (enrichment calls must be no-op or stubbed). - Cold-start: guard minimum sample sizes before evaluating; auto-promote with warmed caches only after a warmup window. - Privacy/compliance: experiments that touch customer PII require opt-in and are blocked by default in Private deployments.

APIs & Console UX: - Experiment API: createExperiment(spec) / start / pause / stop / status / results. Spec includes metrics (name, type: binary/continuous, direction), windows, alpha, min_samples, exposure_schedule, cohorts, rollout_strategy (ramp/instant), and safety_gates. - Console workflows: one-click create from model page, visual traffic schedule editor, live evaluation panel showing top-level signal and per-variant breakdown, and an incidents panel for auto-rollbacks. - Alerts: configurable Slack/PagerDuty hooks for safety veto or unexpected regressions.

Success criteria: - Beta teams can create and run experiments end-to-end without SRE intervention in <= 30 minutes. - Auto-rollback correctly triggers in simulated regressions with >95% recall for injected safety faults in staging. - Mean time-to-detect real regressions reduces by 50% vs current ad hoc experiments.
acceptance_criteria: API to create and run an experiment with variants and an exposure schedule exists and is documented
Runtime enforces traffic split for ramped and instant schedules and supports shadowing with rate limits
Statistical sentry runs sequential checks every evaluation window and emits pass/warn/fail decisions
Auto-rollback executes deterministic rollback, creates an incident record, and notifies configured channels
Console shows live per-variant metrics and a clearly labeled safety dashboard
End-to-end test injecting a quality regression in staging triggers sentry and rollback in expected timeframe
comments: 2025-02-12 Maya Chen: Scoped initial requirements and aligned on project goals with Eng and SRE. Identified two principal analysis modes (frequentist sequential and Bayesian).
2025-02-18 Mateo Rivera: Kicked off design workshop; Eng (Priya, Daniel), SRE (Omar) joined. Action: prototype router hook and define metrics schema.
2025-02-25 Priya (Eng) feedback: Prefer conservative defaults (O'Brien-Fleming) for early rollouts. Flagged cache-bias risk; added requirement to report cache-hit stratified metrics.
2025-03-01 SRE (Omar) feedback: Shadow traffic must be throttled per-variant and must never trigger external side-effects. Also requested circuit-breaker for downstream timeouts.
2025-03-02 Mateo Rivera: Decided auto-rollback will be an opt-in property per-experiment with an explicit audit acceptance in Console. Next: implement sentry MVP and console live panel.
